text:
Joel Eriksson Ek gave Minnesota a scare on Nov. 12, leaving the win over Toronto after a hard collision. He was cleared two days later and answered Tuesday with a goal and three assists against Nashville, his best night of the season.

He is the Wild's heavy-minutes center behind the stars, drawing the other team's best players, and the chances around him are excellent: 57% of the expected goals at five on five, 6.6 points better than the Wild without him. His own shooting is the odd part. Seven goals on 11.7 expected is a shortfall, and he keeps getting the looks (1.59 expected goals per 60, his highest rate in years), so we'd expect more to go in.

The other side of it balances out. His team has scored 6.6 more goals than its chances with him on the ice, which is padding his 21 points. His minutes have also dipped, to 17:37 over the last ten from 19:07 on the season. Put the two together and he's about who he's been: a strong two-way center on a team riding a hot run.
